2609.20419.title: SCGFM-ART: Amortized Relational Transport for Structure-Centric Graph Foundation Models
2609.20419.paper_summary: Graph foundation models (GFMs) aim to learn transferable representations across severely heterogeneous graph domains. However, severe domain shifts in topology, graph scale, and feature semantics impede the construction of a unified, domain-agnostic representation space. To address this, we propose SCGFM-ART, a structure-centric GFM framework that aligns arbitrary graphs onto a shared relational atlas via Amortized Relational Transport (ART). The relational atlas serves as a universal coordinate system defined by a finite set of relational landmarks (bases), while ART directly predicts reusable, end-to-end graph-to-base transport plans, bypassing costly runtime Gromov-Wasserstein optimizations. Under this formulation, SCGFM-ART decomposes a graph into a unified representation: globally via its relational response coordinates relative to the atlas, and locally via its node-to-role structural correspondences. These correspondences project disparate node attributes into a canonical role space, resolving structural and semantic heterogeneity within a singular alignment interface. Rigorously modeling graphs and atlas bases as finite measured relational spaces, we establish coordinate fidelity bounds, prove stability under predicted transport plans, and derive an amortized coverage bound that guarantees our learning objective tightly surrogates ideal relational coverage. Benchmarked across 14 cross-domain graph- and node-level classification tasks, SCGFM-ART achieves state-of-the-art transferability, securing superior average ranks of 2.29 and 1.14, respectively. Topological perturbation analyses demonstrate that node-role transport retains fine-grained structural nuances beyond global coordinates. On real-world benchmarks, the amortized formulation yields 44.2 to 85.1 times faster frozen target-domain inference by avoiding iterative alignment at test time.
2609.20419.paper_summary_zh: 圖形基礎模型（GFMs）旨在學習可轉移的表示，跨越極為異質的圖形領域。<lb/>然而，拓撲、圖形規模和特徵語義的嚴重領域轉變妨礙了統一的、與領域無關的表示空間的構建。<lb/>為了解決這個問題，我們提出了SCGFM-ART，一個以結構為中心的GFM框架，通過經濟關係運輸（ART）將任意圖形對齊到共享的關係圖譜上。<lb/>關係圖譜作為一個由有限的關係標誌（基礎）定義的通用坐標系，而ART則直接預測可重用的端到端圖形到基礎的運輸計劃，繞過了昂貴的運行時Gromov-Wasserstein優化。<lb/>在這種表述下，SCGFM-ART將圖形分解為統一的表示：全球上通過其相對於圖譜的關係響應坐標，局部上通過其節點到角色的結構對應。<lb/>這些對應將不同的節點屬性投影到一個典範角色空間，解決了單一對齊界面內的結構和語義異質性。<lb/>嚴格地將圖形和圖譜基礎建模為有限測量的關係空間，我們建立了坐標保真度界限，證明了在預測運輸計劃下的穩定性，並推導出一個經濟的覆蓋界限，保證我們的學習目標緊密地替代理想的關係覆蓋。<lb/>在14個跨領域圖形和節點級分類任務中進行基準測試，SCGFM-ART實現了最先進的可轉移性，分別獲得了2.29和1.14的優越平均排名。<lb/>拓撲擾動分析表明，節點角色運輸保留了超越全球坐標的細粒度結構細節。<lb/>在現實世界的基準測試中，經濟的表述通過避免測試時的迭代對齊，實現了44.2到85.1倍更快的凍結目標領域推斷。
